verdict.reasoning: Patient reports diarrhea for three days and multiple vomiting episodes: 'Three days ago now' and 'I've been throwing up... I've just been throwing up everything.'
Patient states, 'It's very loose, but it started as being very watery' and 'Today alone, I've been at least four times.'
Patient says, 'I've been throwing up. I can't seem to be able to keep anything in me. Not even water, not even my tea, not even any liquid stuff.'
Patient reports, 'I was sick just after trying... to have breakfast this morning, so maybe about two hours ago.'
Patient: 'Yes, I've been running at serious temperature. I'm literally boiling.' and 'No, because I've not got one [thermometer].'

Patient describes pain 'towards my navel area... I can't touch my navel area. It's just so sore' and later that it 'comes, I feel the strong urge to go to the loo and then sort of releases me... it comes and goes.'
Patient confirms urination 'At least an hour ago' and 'No blood' when asked about blood in stool or urine.
In response to blood in stool/urine: Patient says, 'No blood.'
Patient: 'my brother has actually been having similar symptoms for the past few days as well. And he does say, like, everyone in school's got it... So you've been in contact with him? Yes.'

Patient: 'I've tried the ORs... The salt, sugar mix.' and 'I've taken that, like three times a day for the past two days.' and 'I've been vomiting literally everything I take, so I doubt that even that has had the chance to work.'
When asked about other problems: 'No previous abdominal pains before I get the odd, you know, menstrual cramps and all that.' No other medical issues are described.
Patient states, 'Well, I take my vitamins, Vitamin D every day. That's about all that I regularly take.'
Patient: 'I only take vitamins for my menstrual cramps when it comes. Maybe I might take a naprine just to eat the pain.'
When asked about smoking: 'Well, I don't smoke.'
Same line: 'but, you know, I have a pint from time to time.'
Patient: 'I'm a graphics designer.' and 'I'm working from home today because I can't.'
When asked who she lives with: 'I live with my brother and my mum.'
Patient answers: 'No.' to 'Are you on any contraception?' and 'No.' to 'Are you having regular sexual intercourse?'

Doctor states, 'it sounds like it might be an infectious gastroenteritis that you've got, which is usually caused by a virus,' in context of three days of diarrhea and vomiting and contact with brother/school outbreak.
Doctor: 'we should also check that you're not getting dehydrated because if you're not keeping fluid down that you can get dehydrated' and notes she is vomiting everything.
Matches earlier HPI: periumbilical pain 'towards my navel area... so sore' that 'comes... I feel the strong urge to go to the loo and then... releases me.'
Patient reports feverishness ('I've been running at serious temperature. I'm literally boiling.') without a measurement, consistent with subjective fever.

Doctor: 'we can make you an urgent appointment and then you can... get the sample sent off and we can check your hydration.' and later confirms booking via support line; patient replies, 'Yes, please.'

Doctor mentions stool sample 'so we can make sure that you haven't got a nasty bacterial infection which needs specific treatment' but does not mention 'culture and MC&S' explicitly or detail targeted therapy steps.
Doctor advises, 'keep going with the rehydration salts. Just tiny sips constantly so that your stomach doesn't get overfilled and you vomit. So just tiny, tiny sips.'

Doctor: 'just have very simple food. If you're going to have anything like two toast or biscuit or something really light like that. Avoid fruit, vegetables, milk, anything like that, which might just make it worse.'
Doctor states, 'if in the meantime you're feeling more unwell, then we would get you seen urgently in ae,' but does not mention specific signs like tachypnea, oliguria, dizziness, or IV fluids.
Doctor provides safety-net: 'if in the meantime you're feeling more unwell, then we would get you seen urgently in ae' and 'So you could call us back in the meantime.'
